newsitem.title: INDIA: India eyeing $5 bln World Bank highway loan - paper.
newsitem.headline: India eyeing $5 bln World Bank highway loan - paper.

text.p: An Indian newspaper said on Tuesday that the Finance Ministry was negotiating a $5 billion loan from the World Bank for the upgrading and building of some 13,000 km (8,000 miles) of highways.
The Financial Express said the ministry estimated average annual inflow of $500 million of World Bank financing over 10 years for state highways.
The business daily said the final details of the loan would be discussed at a meeting set for next week in Washington between Finance Ministry and World Bank officials.
A World Bank spokesman in New Delhi said he had no information on the reported loan. Finance Ministry officials were unavailable for comment.
The Financial Express said the World Bank was insisting that the 16 states which would receive the highway financing should contribute 30 percent of the cost of the highway project.
The World Bank is especially interested in helping upgrade state highways as a means of alleviating pressure on overburdened national roads, the newspaper said.
